rules: Pac-Man starts at (7,4) every episode; a pellet (+1) on every other open cell (47 pellets, including under the ghosts).
Two ghosts start at (2,4) and (2,5) with a random initial heading.

Ghosts move one cell every second step (half Pac-Man's speed), never reversing unless forced; on each move a ghost takes the step that minimises maze (BFS) distance to Pac-Man with prob 0.7, otherwise a random legal non-reversing step.
Step order: ghosts move (on their steps), then Pac-Man moves (moves into walls leave him in place, no-op stays); Pac-Man dies if he ends on a ghost cell or swaps cells with a ghost.
Eating a pellet gives +1; death gives -1 and ends the episode; eating the last pellet ends the episode (no clear bonus); 200-step cap.
Observation: ch0 Pac-Man, ch1 ghosts, ch2 pellets, ch3 walls (ring + maze), ch4 previous Pac-Man+ghost cells (at reset = the current cells).

notes: Structure (maze, fixed starts, 2 half-speed ghosts that mostly chase, +1 pellet / -1 death / end on clear, prev-frame at reset = current cells) is well supported: TD residual drops from ~1.4 (random starts) and ~0.6 (random ghosts) to ~0.27, and critic V(s0) matches the empirical discounted return only with these starts and prev0='same'. Not pinned down: the ghosts' chase probability (0.6-1.0 all plausible; 1.0 gives a lower TD residual but return 47 and random length 16, so 0.7 was chosen on the joint fit), tie-breaking and exact ghost targeting rule (BFS vs Manhattan nearly indistinguishable), initial ghost headings. Our trained policy uses no-op ~2x more often than the reference (0.065 vs 0.034); sampled return is ~5% above the reference. FOLLOW-UP PASS (pm_next.py, pm_rules.py, pm_noop.py): computed the critic's policy-expected Bellman residual per state for exact ghost-rule distributions (removes sampling noise). It does not single out a ghost rule: chase prob 0-1, BFS vs Manhattan, reversal allowed or not, and alternate-step vs every-step timing all land at 0.24-0.30 (alternate, chase 0.7: 0.26; every step, chase 0: 0.24). The ~0.25 floor is far above Breakout's 0.005, so something is still off; it is not the ghost rule alone. Pellet reward 1 is confirmed: 0.5 and 0.7 give 0.43 and 0.31. No-op gap: our extra no-ops are spread across contexts, mostly when ghosts are 3-4 cells away, and grow with ghost randomness. Ghosts moving every step bring no-op down to 0.035-0.045 (ref .034), but the sampled TD residual rises to ~0.59 and the return falls to 37-38, so the fit is worse. Kept BEST unchanged. Verdict downgraded to approximate: the always-chasing variant has a lower sampled residual (0.18) yet misses the return and random length, and the residual floor suggests an unidentified rule difference.
